newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-Market seen resting after run-up.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-Market seen resting after run-up.

text.p: Initial public offerings will slack off a bit this week with lighter volumes and smaller premiums after a stellar performance last week featuring high-flyers Ciena Corp, Vail Resorts, and Yurie Systems Inc

IPOs raised $1.5 billion last week, topping the past nine weeks, according to Securities Data Co. And because demand surged, six of the last nine deals priced at the high end or above their estimated price range.

But below the fireworks was a disturbing trend. Some of the large IPOs lost most of their initial gains, including Circuit City Group's used car business CarMax. On Friday Vail's highly-touted IPO "broke issue" -- or fell below its IPO price of $22 despite first day gains.
"The market is really paying more for growth now and not name recognition," said Ken Fleming, an IPO analyst at Renaissance Capital Corp of Greenwich, Conn.
Another contributing factor to the losses, said IPO Aftermarket editor John Fitzgibbon, is that prices were too far above initial expectations, shaving anticipated premiums.
"They can shipwreck these stocks by squeezing all the juice out of them and into the pockets of the underwriters," Fitzgibbon said.

IPO analysts expected the market to bounce back after a winter hibernation period but some were surprised at just how big the bounce was. Still, they were cautious to point out that the mood continues to remain far more selective than last spring, when speculative fervor gripped the IPO market.
This week, contact lens-maker Wesley-Jessen VisionCare Inc, Qualix Group Inc, and Daou Systems could possibly be good investments, Fleming said.

Fitzgibbon said he expected few fireworks this week except from Apex PC Solutions, which could have gains of 1.5 to 2 points after its opening, and possibly Daou. Wesley-Jessen could rise about 1/2 point or slightly more, he said.
"But there are homeruns in the calendar in the future," he said.
According to Securities Data, 156 companies have registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for offerings that would raise about $3.5 billion.
